svg.title: Three layers, each aimed at a different adversary
svg.text: Layer 1
Fraud and account takeover
Mostly automated and untargeted. This
is the one that costs people money.
What to do
A password manager, a
different password per site
Two-factor authentication, the
strongest method available
Keep the system and browser updated
Switch channel to confirm
any message that rushes you
How long
About an hour. Start with email,
then banking and messaging
Layer 2
Commercial data collection
Platforms, advertisers and data brokers, running
continuously and not aimed at you personally.
What to do
Phone permissions and the
advertising identifier
Full-disk encryption and a boot password
End-to-end encryption for everyday messaging
Backups, and a restore you have actually tested
An account inventory
How long
A few evenings. One item at a time,
no need to finish it in one sitting
Layer 3
Targeted investigation
Backed by legal process or technical
resources. Most people are not on that list.
What to do
See the section on when to raise your
standard for what triggers this layer
How long
Depends. Changing identity or device changes
which records can be linked, nothing more
Overrated measures, each with a
use, none the main line of defence
A VPN changes who can see your connection.
Private browsing clears local traces while
platforms and your ISP still recognise you.
NIST no longer asks for scheduled password
changes. A recycled phone number gets
reassigned, so unlink the old accounts first.
A camera sticker works on the camera, while
most people are worried about the microphone.
Deleting an app stops future collection only.
